annotationRationale: The angle-bisector side ratio determines both trapezoid bases. Similar-triangle area scaling finds the remaining trapezoid's area, and the trapezoid formula establishes the 5/6 area ratio. The midsegment theorem supplies the parallel lines and similarity.
sourceMethod: Follows the official comparison of two trapezoids with a common height. It explicitly applies the Angle Bisector Theorem in both triangles and writes the area-formula ratio.

review.mathCheck: The angle-bisector ratios give DF/DE = BG/BC = 5/6. Similarity gives area(ADE) = 120/4 = 30, so the common-height trapezoid comparison gives area(FDBG) = (5/6)(120−30) = 75, choice D. This holds for both admissible triangle configurations.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithfully rewords MAA solution 24 on page 12: compare the two trapezoids using the 5/6 base ratios and remove the quarter-area triangle. The added area-formula calculation explains the official comparison.
review.annotationCheck: Self-contained for AMC 10. The parallel bases and common height are justified, and the argument does not depend on the source figure's scale or angle configuration.
